userJob: Place the price so a buyer never has to search for it
problem: The price is revealed on interaction, on a later step, or only inside a variant selector, so the buyer's first question is answered last
worksWhen: Anywhere the object appears: listing row, card, detail page, configurator step, basket line
avoidWhen: Price genuinely does not exist yet, in which case the page says so in words rather than hiding the absence
mechanism: The price is locatable without search wherever the object appears. Three shapes that satisfy it differently: one column of a dense listing in the same position every row; carried on the object's own label inside the photograph; spoken in the configurator's sentence as the choices change. A reduction names a figure the object actually sold at, and no former price is invented.
risks: Showing a from-price that no configuration can reach, which the buyer discovers at the total
Hiding the price behind a variant choice, which makes the choice a toll rather than a decision
mobileRules: At 375px the price stays in the same relationship to the object after the columns collapse
The figure does not reflow the row when it updates; reserve its width
accessibilityRules: Price is text, not an image, and its currency is stated rather than implied by symbol placement alone
A reduced price and its former figure are distinguishable without relying on strike-through colour
genericnessNote: The obligation names locatability, and the three shapes it offers produce visibly different pages.

userJob: Make it unmistakable which control actually buys the thing
problem: Three controls of similar weight sit near each other, so add to basket, save for later and compare all look like the commitment and none of them reads as it
worksWhen: Any surface where a transaction can start
avoidWhen: A page that deliberately offers no commitment, such as a specification archive; adding one there is a false affordance
mechanism: Exactly one control acquires the object and cannot be mistaken for another, and it is reachable from anywhere the buyer might decide. Three ways to make the distinction: the only filled control among outlines; alone in its band behind a rule at any weight; repeated at the close of every section. Reserving a colour for it is one answer, not the answer.
risks: Two calls to action with the same intent under different labels, which splits the decision
A persistent bar at 375px that covers the content the buyer is deciding from
mobileRules: Reachable from anywhere usually means a persistent control at 375px, with bottom inset reserved so it never covers the last row of content
44px target with 24px clearance from any adjacent control
accessibilityRules: The control is a real button or link with a name that says what happens, and the name stays the same across the page
Focus order reaches it without traversing the whole specification
genericnessNote: The default expression is one filled brand-coloured button, so the distinction has to be argued from the page's own weight rather than assumed.

userJob: Show everything the buyer is agreeing to at the moment they agree
problem: Delivery cost, delivery time, stock state and return terms are on four other pages, so the total only becomes true at the last step and the buyer leaves there
worksWhen: Any commitment moment: add to basket, start checkout, confirm order, start a subscription
avoidWhen: Never; if a term is genuinely unknown, the page says which term and why
mechanism: Everything the buyer pays, waits for and may return is readable at the moment of commitment without navigating away. Stock, offer and delivery state are in words rather than colour alone, and are settled before checkout. Three shapes: a panel holding price, variant, delivery cost and time; one sentence naming what is paid, the wait and what may be returned; a confirm page restating it before anything is charged.
risks: Stating a delivery time the business has not committed to, which is a claim the customer will hold them to
Collapsing the terms into a link labelled details, which moves the information off the surface
mobileRules: At 375px the panel is usually the last thing above the commit control; keep it there rather than in an accordion the buyer must open
accessibilityRules: The terms are announced with the commitment, not only visible near it
Stock state is a word, never a coloured dot alone
genericnessNote: What the terms are comes from the business, so the panel's content differs per client by construction.

userJob: Update a price, a basket or a total without animating it
problem: A total counts up, a basket badge bounces, or a recalculation shows a spinner, so the figure the buyer is trying to read is the one thing in motion
worksWhen: Every price, basket line, delivery estimate and total, on every commerce surface
avoidWhen: Never; a slow server is answered with a written line, not with movement on the figure
mechanism: No figure animates on a price, in the basket or at checkout. Adding, filtering and recalculating delivery each answer inside a tenth of a second, whatever the server takes. Three ways: the figure is simply different on the next paint; a written line states what changed while the figures hold still; the control rewrites its own word to the completed one.
risks: Answering locally and then correcting when the server disagrees, which is worse than waiting
Using a skeleton on the price, which is an animation on the figure by another name
mobileRules: A bouncing basket badge is more disruptive at 375px where it sits next to the commit control
Reserve the figure's width so a longer total does not reflow the row
accessibilityRules: A change to a total is announced through a polite live region so it is not silent for a screen reader user
The control that rewrites its own word keeps the same accessible name pattern, so Add becomes Added rather than a new control
genericnessNote: Stillness near money removes a class of effects rather than prescribing a look.

userJob: Build filtering that runs on the words the buyer already uses
problem: Facets are lifted from the warehouse taxonomy, so the buyer is asked to choose a product family code when what they know is the size of their kitchen
worksWhen: A catalogue large enough that the buyer cannot see all of it, which is where narrowing earns its cost
avoidWhen: A small set the buyer can read in full, where filters add a step and remove the overview
mechanism: Narrowing runs on the buyer's own nouns, not the warehouse's. The count is always known, an empty result offers the nearest thing that exists, and the buyer returns with filters intact. What they have gathered stays reachable. Three shapes: named facets over a dense result with the count above and the state in the address; one question at a time reducing a stated remainder, each step re-enterable; a written index of categories with sizes and a line of what is held.
risks: Filters that do not survive the back button, which throws away the buyer's work
A zero result with no nearest alternative, which ends the visit
mobileRules: At 375px filters usually move behind a control; the active count stays visible on that control so the buyer knows the set is narrowed
Applying a filter must not lose scroll position in the result
accessibilityRules: The result count is announced when it changes, not only rendered
Filter state is reachable and removable by keyboard, including clearing all of them
genericnessNote: Facet chrome converges, but the nouns come from the buyer's own trade and cannot be reused across clients.

userJob: Show a product so the buyer knows what size it is and what it looks like from more than one side
problem: One studio shot on white at one angle tells the buyer the colour and nothing else, so the return is the size check
worksWhen: Physical goods, and any object whose scale is not obvious from its name
avoidWhen: An intangible product, where photography would be decoration and a diagram or a screen is the honest asset
mechanism: More than one angle, treated alike across the catalogue, with scale established explicitly. Three ways: studio shots treated alike with dimensions written on each frame; objects held, worn or in use so a body carries the scale; measured drawings to a stated scale where no shot exists. Where the real photograph does not exist, a labelled placeholder naming subject, crop and ground is a finished answer and a generated one is not.
risks: Mixing treatments across the catalogue, so two products cannot be compared by eye
Generating an image of a real object, which is a claim about a thing that exists
mobileRules: At 375px the second angle is usually below the fold; make the existence of further angles visible rather than only swipeable
Reserve each frame's aspect ratio so the gallery does not shift as images load
accessibilityRules: Each frame carries alt text saying what the angle shows, not the product name repeated
A gallery is operable by keyboard and its current position is stated
genericnessNote: Treatment is free and scale can be carried by a body, a rule, a coin or a drawing, so the answers diverge.

userJob: Make each selling claim resolvable without leaving the page
problem: The page carries benefits with nothing behind them, so a buyer who wants to verify one has to leave, and the specification that would have answered them is curated down to the flattering rows
worksWhen: Any surface making claims about a product, a service or a result
avoidWhen: Never; where proof is absent, the page says so and why, which is still an answer
mechanism: Each claim resolves to a specification line on the same surface, and a benefit without one is cut. Every specification that exists is shown, grouped when there are many, never curated. Proof carries its size, spread and worst cases, because a mean from three is not a mean from three hundred. Where proof is absent, name the absence and its reason.
risks: Showing a mean without its count, which reads as stronger evidence than it is
Grouping specifications in a way that quietly drops the unflattering rows
mobileRules: Grouped specifications at 375px need their group headings visible; an accordion that hides every group hides the whole proof
accessibilityRules: A specification is a real table or definition list with headers, not a grid of divs
A claim that links to its row moves focus to that row, not merely scrolls to it
genericnessNote: The proof comes from the client's own data, so this obligation cannot produce two identical pages.

userJob: Decide what to remove from a commerce page before shipping it
problem: Sections accumulate because each one seemed reasonable alone, so the page ends up with three trust strips, two newsletter blocks and a related-products row between the buyer and the commit control
worksWhen: At the end of any commerce build, before the render matrix
avoidWhen: Never; the audit is cheap and its output is a list of removals rather than a redesign
mechanism: Go through every element on the page and name it as either helping the purchase or in its way. Then remove the second list. The output is written down, so the removals can be challenged rather than rediscovered on the next build.
risks: Classifying a slow-burn element such as returns policy as in the way, when it is what makes the commitment legible
Removing everything that is not a control, which strips the page of the evidence the claims need
mobileRules: Run the audit against the 375px order, since the mobile stack is where an interruption between decision and commit costs most
accessibilityRules: Removals must not take away a landmark or a skip target that navigation depends on
genericnessNote: An audit removes rather than adds, so it cannot introduce a house style.

userJob: Decide what to do when the brief has no scarcity, stock pressure or countdown to show
problem: A page feels flat without urgency, so a counter, a low-stock badge or a limited-run line gets added from nothing, and it is a claim the customer can hold the business to
worksWhen: Every commerce build where real scarcity data does not exist
avoidWhen: Real, current scarcity exists and is readable from the client's own system, where stating it is honest
mechanism: If it is not in the brief or the evidence, it does not go on the page, not as a placeholder and not as a plausible example. When the sentence is needed and the fact is missing, ask for it or cut the sentence. A page with no scarcity claim is honest and an invented one is not. Voice is yours to invent, facts are not.
risks: Treating a plausible number as a placeholder that someone will replace later, which nobody does
Softening the invention into a vague phrase, which is the same claim with less to check
mobileRules: No mobile-specific exception; a badge that only appears at 375px is the same invention
accessibilityRules: A real scarcity statement is text with its as-of time, not a colour or an animated counter
genericnessNote: Refusing to invent removes a whole class of interchangeable furniture from the page.
